questions.question: In the context of digital marketing, a 'customer journey' maps which of the following?

options.text: The physical location of each customer
The series of interactions and touchpoints a customer has from awareness to purchase and beyond
The shipping route from warehouse to customer
The internal process of manufacturing the product

questions.explanation: The digital customer journey tracks all interactions — from first discovering a brand to post-purchase advocacy — helping companies optimise each touchpoint.

questions.question: Which sales strategy involves a small number of high-value clients and typically requires long, relationship-driven sales cycles?

options.text: High-velocity inside sales
Enterprise or key account sales
Self-serve e-commerce
Viral referral programmes

questions.explanation: Enterprise sales targets a small number of large accounts with high contract values. It involves consultative selling, multiple stakeholders, and long negotiation cycles.

questions.question: Which is a key distinction between B2B and B2C buying behaviour?

options.text: B2B purchases are always smaller in value than B2C purchases
B2B purchases typically involve multiple stakeholders, longer cycles, and more rational evaluation criteria
Emotional appeal is more important than logic in B2B decisions
B2B and B2C buying behaviour are identical

questions.explanation: B2B purchases involve buying committees, defined procurement processes, long evaluation cycles, and emphasis on ROI and risk reduction rather than impulse or emotion.

questions.question: Content marketing as a promotional strategy primarily works by:

options.text: Broadcasting paid advertisements to mass audiences
Creating valuable, relevant content that attracts and engages a target audience organically
Offering aggressive discounts on all products
Sponsoring large sporting events

questions.explanation: Content marketing builds authority and trust by providing genuinely useful content (articles, videos, podcasts) that draws potential customers through organic search and sharing.

questions.question: The FinTech customer journey case study primarily illustrates which marketing challenge?

options.text: The low cost of customer acquisition in financial services
Building trust and reducing friction at every digital touchpoint in a regulated, high-stakes industry
Why FinTech companies should avoid digital channels
The ease of retaining customers in financial services

questions.explanation: FinTech faces unique challenges in building customer trust, navigating regulatory requirements, and reducing friction in onboarding — every journey touchpoint must build confidence.

questions.question: Which factor is most important when choosing between different sales channels for a startup?

options.text: Whichever channel is used by the largest competitor
Where the target customer actually discovers and purchases products in this category
The channel with the lowest one-time setup cost regardless of ongoing performance
The channel that requires the most intermediaries

questions.explanation: Channel selection must align with actual customer behaviour — where they search, evaluate, and buy — not simply mirror competitors or minimise setup costs.

questions.question: Penetration pricing sets a low initial price primarily to:

options.text: Signal premium quality to early adopters
Rapidly acquire market share and deter competitors
Recover R&D investment immediately at launch
Charge different prices to different customer segments simultaneously

questions.explanation: Penetration pricing uses a low price to quickly attract a large user base, establish market presence, and create barriers for competitors through scale and switching costs.

questions.question: Which metric is most directly used to measure the efficiency of customer acquisition efforts?

options.text: Gross Margin
Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
Net Promoter Score (NPS)
Return on Equity (ROE)

questions.explanation: CAC measures the total cost (marketing + sales) divided by the number of new customers acquired, indicating how efficiently the business converts spend into customers.
